result.topic_en: Riemann discusses how a fall or rise in external temperature might affect the auditory ossicles relative to the walls of the tympanic cavity, concludes this cannot be settled given ignorance of the thermal properties of the components, and announces a section IV on the positional changes of the ossicles under a temperature change.

items.english: The tympanic cavity will in consequence cool noticeably, the surrounding bones only very little, and the ossicles will contract noticeably while the walls of the tympanic cavity remain almost unchanged.

items.english: Beyond the fact that the ossicles cool and contract much more strongly than the walls of the tympanic cavity when the external temperature falls, little more can be established about the influence of temperature on the tympanic apparatus, given our complete ignorance of the thermal properties of its components.
